sections.title: Introduction
Typical working process
Obtaining access to Arena
sections.text:
Arena platform is available at https://www.openforis-arena.org
Every user in the Arena platform has a specific role. These roles are described in detail in this chapter.
The platform limitations are as follows:
* The service is free and the maximum size of survey data is 10 GB.
* Only the Survey Administrator can view the survey data size.
* The maximum upload size of any file is limited to 1 GB.
In general, it is better to avoid uploading very-high resolution images into Arena, and to plan the amount of incoming data.
There are two methods to get access to Arena:
Method 1. Become a Survey Manager[2].
As a Survey Manager can create a new survey and tailor it to meet your needs.
You can also use ready-made templates to tailor your survey.
To become a Survey Manager, go to https://www.openforis-arena.org/
and request access to the Arena platform.

You will next see the following page:

Fill in all information. If you are dealing with forest resource data or are a first-time user with no experience with Open Foris Collect, it is recommended to start using a template: read more about them in this Annex. Then send the request and wait for approval. It takes typically 1-3 working days until you get an invitation to access the Arena platform. When you have the access rights to Arena, your role will be a Survey Administrator for your first survey.
Method 2. To get access to an existing survey, ask for an invitation from the Survey Administrator. This person can send you an invitation to new users by email. The Survey Administrator will specify your role in the survey.

When you have access to Arena, type in your email and password. In case you have forgotten your password, there is an option to receive a new temporary password by email.

If you are a new user, set first your User Profile (My Profile). On the upper-right side of the screen there is a blank icon and entry to the user profile details.
Here you can set up the following details: Title, Name (i.e., username), Email, and (access) Group. In addition, you can add an image for your user profile.

sections.title: Selecting and creating a survey (1/2)
sections.text:
In the upper right corner, there is access to the following functions:

My Surveys section shows a table with all accessible surveys to the user. The list contains the following details.
Header
	Explanation
	NAME
	Name of the survey. It must be at least 6 letters long.
	LABEL
	Label for the survey
	OWNER
	Name of survey administrator (owner)
	DATE CREATED
	Date when the survey was created
	DATE LAST MODIFIED
	Date when the survey was edited last time
	DATE PUBLISHED
	Date when the survey was published
	STATUS
	Draft:                   The survey is at the editing stage. It contains no data.
Published:           The survey is ready to store data. It can contain input data.
Published-Draft: The survey is ‘published’, but there are unpublished changes
                             in its structure (i.e., changes in attribute properties, new
                             calculation scripts or setting).
	NODES
	Number of nodes. This indicates the size of the survey.
	CYCLES
	Number of cycles in the survey.
	LANGUAGES
	Languages in the survey (ISO 639 language codes)
	RECORDS
	Number of records in the survey (across all cycles)
	FILES
	Number of uploaded files (e.g. photos)
	CHAINS
	Number of processing chains in the survey

   Click this button to see or hide some columns!
New Survey allows a Survey Manager to create a survey in three ways:
1) Create a new survey from scratch, 2) Clone an existing survey or 3) Import a survey (Arena or Collect).
About naming of a survey:
* The name should only contain lower case letters, underscores,
* No space,
* No special characters (#%&"?).
The entry box will automatically ignore the wrong letters.
Next, some more information on how to create a new survey.
Method 1: Create a new survey from scratch.
Fill in Name, Label, and choose the default language.

Next steps after creating a new survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and set in Description, needed Spatial Reference System(s) (SRS) and survey languages.
* Create the survey structure using the Survey Designer, test your survey and then finally Publish it.

Method 2: Clone a survey from an existing survey.
Fill in a new survey Name and select a survey to be cloned. Cloning will only copy the survey structure, not the data.  A cloned survey will always be in the ‘draft’ mode.

Next steps after cloning the survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed.
* If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then Publish it.

Method 3: Import a survey.
Import offers two options:
a) Import an Arena survey (.zip). An existing Arena survey, such as an Arena backup, can be imported back into Arena (with a new name).
b) Import an Open Foris Collect survey.

Give first the name of the new survey in Arena. Check the Include Data box if the survey file contains data and needs to be imported, otherwise leave it unchecked.

Important: Do not use Export + Import (schema or backup) for cloning a survey! The reason is that a published and exported survey will stay published when imported back into Arena. This means that only a few changes are possible. Instead, if you clone a survey, the new survey will be in the draft mode, and you can, for example, change/edit a taxonomic list.

Next steps after importing the survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties if needed.
* If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then Publish it.

An Open Foris Collect survey can be imported from a .collect, .collect-backup or .collect-data file. Note that after importing you should view the Collect Import Report at the Dashboard section. In addition, check out that all forms, tables, attributes and their properties are imported correctly.
Follow these steps after importing a Collect survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed.

sections.title: Branding
sections.text:
The ‘Branding’ tab lets survey designers customize the visual identity of a survey: its primary color, up to three logos, a background image for the survey landing page, and typography presets for the landing page title and description. Branding settings are saved with the survey and are published together with the rest of the survey definition, so data collectors and reviewers see the same branding once the survey is published.
Branding is entirely optional. A survey with no branding configured still displays a functional, unbranded landing page.
The Branding tab is organized as a form on the top and a live preview of the survey landing page on the bottom, so changes to colors, logos, background, and typography can be checked before saving.

Survey landing page
Branding is applied on the survey landing page, which is the default view when opening a survey from Home. The landing page shows the survey title and description (from the survey labels), a button to go to Records, and, when configured, the survey's branding: primary color, logos, background image, and typography presets. A separate button opens the Dashboard, which has moved to its own top-level module in the sidebar.
Primary color
The primary color is the main accent color for the survey. It is applied to key interface elements such as primary buttons and sidebar highlights, both on the survey landing page and while collecting data, so the tool matches the branding of the project or organization running the survey.
Set the primary color using the color picker or by entering a hex value directly (for example, #2E7D32). If an invalid color value is entered, the field shows a validation error and the branding form cannot be saved until it is corrected.
Typography presets
Typography presets control the text size of the survey title and description as they appear on the landing page. Choose the preset that best fits the length of the survey title and description and the overall look of the branding.
Logos
Up to three logos can be uploaded (Logo 1, Logo 2, and Logo 3). All three are optional and independent of each other.
Logo slot
	Typical use
	Displayed on
	Logo 1
	Main survey / project logo
	Survey landing page and header
	Logo 2
	Partner or implementing organization logo
	Survey landing page
	Logo 3
	Additional partner, donor, or country logo
	Survey landing page
	To upload a logo, select Upload for the relevant logo slot and choose an image file. Once a logo has been uploaded, the upload button for that slot is replaced by a preview of the image and a delete action; an existing logo must be deleted before a new one can be uploaded in its place. Logos that have been uploaded are shown, in order, on the survey landing page.
Landing page background image
A background image can be uploaded for the survey landing page. Background images are raster images (for example, JPG or PNG) and are limited to 5 MB. Use Upload to add a background image and Delete to remove it; as with logos, an existing background image must be removed before a new one can be uploaded.

sections.title: Document layout
sections.text:
The Document Layout tab is available in Dashboard → Edit info to users who can edit the survey. It contains two groups of settings.
1) Document images
Images can be added to be shown in the header or footer of every printed document. Examples are an organization logo, a project banner, or a footer with contact details.
To add an image, click the + button. In the dialog that opens, set the following fields:
Field
	Explanation
	Label
	Label of the image (required, in at least one survey language).
	Place
	Header or Footer (required).
	Apply if condition
	Optional expression. It is evaluated against the root entity of the record being printed. The image is used only if the condition is met.
	File
	PNG, JPG or SVG image, max. 5 MB. File names must be unique.
	The document contains at most one header image and one footer image. For each place, Arena uses the first image in the list whose "Apply if" condition is met, or which has no condition. This lets you define alternative images for different cases. For example, you could use a different partner logo depending on the region of the record:
* Image 1: Header, Apply if: region == "north"
* Image 2: Header, Apply if: region == "south"
* Image 3: Header, no condition (used when neither of the above applies)
Existing images can be edited with the edit icon or by double-clicking the row. They can be downloaded with the download icon and removed with the trash icon.
2) Layout options
Option
	Default
	Explanation
	Header on first page only
	Enabled
	If enabled, the header image is printed only on the first page. If disabled, it is repeated on every page.
	Page numbering
	Enabled
	If enabled, page numbers are printed on each page.
	Note: as with other survey settings, publish the survey to make changes available to all users.

sections.title: User extra properties
sections.text:
User extra properties section allows defining properties that can be associated with the users working with the survey. These properties can be numeric or text values.

Values can be assigned to the users in the Users list, pressing the  icon at the end of each row; in the dialog that opens, values can be specified for each user extra property:

User extra properties can be used in expressions like default values, validation rules etc., or to filter category items or taxa in the taxon attribute search. The function used to retrieve a user extra property is userProp and it can be used in default values, validation rules, items filter expressions etc.

sections.title: Security
sections.text:
Only a Survey Administrator can view and edit the survey’s Security settings, as follows:

Meaning of “can view not owned records”: If enabled, then a Data Editor/Analyst can view all other users’ records in the survey (on the list of records). If disenabled, a Data Editor/Analyst cannot view other users’ records in the survey.

sections.title: Publish a survey
Export survey and data backup
sections.text:
The survey can be exported into a zip file with or without the data. In this way the user can create and download a backup file. The zip file contains the following content depending on the selected option:
Export                        Export with data (No Activity Log)           Export with data (Backup)

Activity log contains the history of a survey. For example, it can contain data about who and when a certain record attribute was updated with a new value, or who and when a record was upgraded from Cleansing level to Analysis.
It is typically faster to export a survey without the activity log.

A survey containing a calculation chain and result attributes can be exported also without the result attributes.  In this case, the exported file contains the survey structure and the input data.

sections.title: Unpublish or delete a survey
sections.text:
In "Advanced functions", there are methods to unpublish a survey or delete it. Only a Survey Administrator can unpublish or delete a survey. Unpublishing removes all data from the survey but keeps its structure.
Deleting removes both data and the survey structure from the database. To delete a survey, you need to confirm the deletion by typing in the survey name.

After deleting a survey, you have no active survey selected. This means that most commands will be inactivated. If you go to the Home or Dashboard section, you will see the next text on the screen.

In order to continue working with Arena, you either need to select a survey or start creating a new one.

sections.title: Collect Import report
sections.text:
If a survey was imported from an Open Foris Collect file, it gets a Collect Import Report. Otherwise, this option is not visible for a survey.
The main difference between Arena and Collect is that Arena uses JavaScript (JS) language in expressions, but OF Collect uses XPath language (for example within Required and Validation rules). So, when a Collect survey is imported, all expressions need to be converted from XPath into JS, either programmatically or by typing them in manually.
After importing a Collect survey into Arena, the Collect Import Report table shows all expressions which need special attention, such as possible modifications. The import process can convert the most typical XPath expressions into JS, but not complex expressions. Therefore, it is essential to fix all remaining issues before trying to publish an imported survey.

The report table contains the following fields:
PATH:        path of entity/attribute in the survey structure.
TYPE:         expression type (Default value, Validation rule, Relevant if).
EXPRESSION:        expression in Collect (Xpath).
APPLY IF:        XPath APPLY IF expression in OF Collect.
MESSAGES:        Validation rule’s user-tailored message in OF Collect.
    View/Edit messages with other (selected) languages.
RESOLVED:          If blank, the import process did not do the conversion. Check all unsolved issues before publishing your survey! Mark the issue "solved" (manually) after doing the correction.
   Tick shows that the issue is solved.
             Edit the table, form or attribute properties.

The report table can be exported into an Excel file by clicking the Export to Excel button. This is probably the best way to examine what needs to be fixed in the survey. In this table, the value ‘1’  in the column ‘Resolved’ indicates resolved cases, and those with blanks are not converted in the importing process.

Important:
A Collect survey can contain a validation rule which is logically incorrect but still working (!): a value is checked against an attribute that is given later on the form/table. An example: in Collect, the XPath validation expression is given for "Mechantable" (height) as follows:

In this case, the Collect Import Report shows this as an unresolved issue. The reason is that in this survey "tree_height (Height [m])" is after "Mechantable", as seen below in the table. Arena cannot manage a validation expression with an attribute being second in the hierarchy.

The second typical issue with a Collect survey is that Collect may not require setting in the key fields for multiple-entry entities. In Arena, all multiple-entry entities must have a key (or keys).

sections.title: Working with cycles
sections.text:
Arena can host multi-cycle data. By default, all new surveys contain ‘Cycle 1’. Only the Survey Administrator or System Administrator can add, edit or delete cycles in the Dashboard/Survey Info section. Every survey needs to have at least one cycle.
After adding, editing, or deleting a cycle, the survey should be published to make the changes effective. Deleting a cycle will permanently remove all the records of the cycle!
When a new cycle is added, it inherits the survey structure (i.e. schema) from the previous cycle. However, data structure between the cycles can contain differences, so each cycle can have individual properties such as different attributes, form layout, etc.
If the survey contains more than one cycle, an attribute (with a specific name) can belong to one specific cycle, or to preset cycle(s). Attribute’s properties (e.g., name, label, validation rules) are same across the cycles, but an attribute’s position on the forms may vary.

More about cycles:
* Each cycle contains its own records. A record cannot be common across cycles.
* Settings for the Arena Map are common across cycles.
* Categories and taxonomies are common across cycles.
* Chains are common across cycles.
* The Validation Report is executed only for the selected cycle data.
* "Survey Export with Data" will export data (as a backup) from all cycles.
* "Data Export" into CSV/Excel files will export data from the selected cycle. In every table, the first column indicates the cycle number.
* "Data Import" will import data only into the selected cycle.
* Within a published survey, records can be cloned from a cycle to a newer cycle (read more in Cloning data).
* Data processing with Studio can retrieve data from the Arena server only from the selected cycle, not all data across cycles.

sections.title: Survey
sections.text:
The Survey section contains the following tools:
* Form Designer *): tools for creating new data entry forms, creating and editing of tables/forms and attributes and all their properties, and to design the visual outlook of the forms.
* Hierarchy:              Show the survey hierarchy, entities, and attributes.
* Dependency tree: Graphical tool that shows how attributes, calculations, validations, and expressions depend on each other within a survey schema.
* Categories **):   Management of categorical data (i.e. code lists).
* Taxonomies **): Management of taxonomic data (i.e. species lists).
*) This is available for a Survey Administrator.
**) Survey Administrator can add, edit and delete lists, other users can only view them.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.text:
Entity: Data entities are the objects of the data model such as ‘plot’ or ‘tree’. These are shown in Arena as forms or tables. Entities are containers for attributes and relationships between objects.
Attribute: A data attribute is a unit of information inside a data entity, i.e. it is a single-value descriptor for a data object. These are like properties of data entities: for example, an entity ‘tree’ can contain the following attributes: species, diameter, and age.
Node (object): A node is a basic unit of a data structure, and in Arena the data structure has the shape of a tree. A node object is represented by a single node in a tree, and it can be an element node, attribute node, text node, or any "node type"[3].

sections.title: Attribute data types
sections.text:
The properties of an entity (table/form) or an attribute describe the characteristics and behavior of data added to that object. The data type is the most important property because it determines what kind of data the field can store. Arena supports the most common data types applied in database management systems, and two composite data types: coordinates and taxonomic data. The data attribute types are presented in the following table.
Data type

	Notes
	Boolean

yes / no
	Code

	refers to categorical variables (i.e., code lists).
Read more at Categories

Note: Arena creates two fields into the database:
attributename and attributename_label

	allows to enter geographical coordinates
Optional properties: accuracy, altitude, altitude accuracy
	Date

	entered in dd/mm/yyyy format
	Geospatial

	Allows entering geospatial data like polygons. It supports only GeoJSON format.

	File

Optional property (image): show/hide geotag information

Attribute data type conversion is possible. For example, you can change an attribute from Integer to Numeric. However, conversion is possible if the survey has not been published after creating the attribute.   If the survey has been published, and it contains no data (=records), it can be unpublished and a data type can be converted then.
Note 1: When naming attributes, do not use the suffix "_label"! If for example you have a coded attribute cluster_district in the survey, there will (automatically) also be a field cluster_district_label in the database. If there is this type of conflict, this will be shown only when trying to publish the survey.
Note 2: Arena does not contain a data type "range" as applied in OF Collect. When a survey is imported from OF Collect, "range" type attributes are converted into two integer attributes: attributename_from and attributename_to.

sections.title: Description of properties (2/3)
sections.text:
* Enabled: when a taxon is selected using a vernacular (common) name, the specific vernacular name used for the search will also be stored in the data.
* Disabled: only the taxon code and scientific name will be stored, regardless of which vernacular name was used during the search.
In Arena Mobile:
* Enabled: each vernacular name appears as a separate item in the search results list.
* Disabled: all vernacular names for a taxon are grouped together and displayed alongside the taxon (combined in a single entry). As a result, the autocomplete list contains fewer items.
	Vernacular name always included if only one
	* Enabled: If this option is enabled and a taxon has only one vernacular name defined, that vernacular name will automatically be stored with the data when the taxon is selected.
* Disabled: only the taxon code and scientific name will be stored, even if the taxon has a single vernacular name.

	This section is used to add default entry values, and conditions when a form table or attribute is applicable
	Editability:

	* Always editable
	This is the default option; the attribute will always be editable.
	* Editable if condition is met
	If selected, the attribute will be editable only if the specified conditions (expressions) are met.
	* Read Only
	If enabled, the entry can only get the default value (as from an expression)
	Default values:

	* Default values not specified
	Default values will not be applied.
	* Default values specified
	Attribute value will be created using one or more expressions.
Every default value expression is made by an “Expression” and an “Apply if” condition. See more about expressions in Chapter Expressions and expression editor and Examples of expressions.
The first expression for which the “Apply if” condition is met will be applied.
If there are multiple expressions, only the last one can have an empty “Apply if” condition; it will be applied if none of the previous ones are met.
	Default value evaluated only one time
	Disabled: the default value is re-evaluated when the source attributes change.
This selection can cause problems, such as slowness with Arena Mobile.

sections.title: Automatically generating rows from category items
sections.text:
The rows can be automatically generated in a table, where the key attribute is categorical (code). The “Enumerate” can be set to the entity (i.e., to the table):

The rows will be generated using the items defined in the category of the key attribute inside the entity one row for each item). In the enumerated table or form, new rows or forms cannot be added or deleted, and the key code attribute will not be editable. In addition, the key attribute should not have an “Items filter” expression (because the items cannot be changed dynamically).
Note: a code attribute marked as “key” should be defined inside the entity, otherwise marking it with “Enumerate” will not make any effect.

sections.title: Dynamic enumerated entity
sections.text:
Enumerate auto-generates one table row per item in the key attribute's category and disables manual add/delete options. Until now that category always had to be used in full. Dynamic Enumerate adds an optional Enumerating items expression to the entity: when set, only the category items whose code is returned by the expression get a row; the rest are skipped. Leave it empty and Enumerate behaves exactly as before.
The expression is typically built around the unique() function, which returns the distinct values found in a multiple attribute or entity. This lets a table auto-generate one summary row per distinct value already present elsewhere in the record, instead of one row per category item regardless of whether it's used.
Example: a table_source table where the field team logs individual measurements, each tagged with a source_type code and a value:
* table_sum is set to Enumerate, linked to a category “types” (items A, B, C), with Enumerating items expression set to unique(table_source.source_type).
* As the user enters table_source rows, table_sum automatically gains one row for each distinct source_type actually used (not all of A, B, C, only the ones present).
* Each table_sum row can carry its own computed attribute, e.g. value_sum with default value sum(table_source[$context.sum_type == source_type].value), to total the matching entries.

Prerequisites
* The entity already meets the standard Enumerate requirements: multiple-entry table, Enumerate checked, with a categorical (code) key attribute linked to a category.
* The category linked to the key attribute must already contain an item for every code the expression can produce; enumeratingItemsExpression only selects among existing items, it does not create new ones. Values with no matching item are silently skipped.
* Like other node-def expressions, anything the expression references must be reachable from the entity's parent context, and the entity cannot reference itself (self-reference is rejected by validation).
Step-by-step
1. In the Form Designer, select the multiple-entry table and check Enumerate.
2. A new Enumerating items expression field appears directly beneath the Enumerate checkbox.
3. Enter the expression, typically unique(<path to a multiple attribute>) - e.g. unique(table_source.source_type). Leave it empty to keep enumerating every category item, as before.
4. Save the entity. While the expression field holds a value, the Enumerate checkbox is locked on; clear the expression first if you need to switch Enumerate off again.
5. Test in Preview or a draft record: add/remove values in the source attribute the expression reads from, and confirm rows in the enumerated table appear and disappear accordingly.
6. Publish the survey.
Behavior and limitations
* Sync is incremental, by design: adding a new distinct value creates one new row; removing the last row with a given value deletes only that row; rows for values that are still present are left completely untouched, including any data already entered in them. Editing an unrelated attribute does not touch the enumerated rows at all.
* Rows still can't be added or deleted manually, only the generated set changes, and only in response to the expression's source data.
* If the entity itself becomes inapplicable (e.g. via relevant when expression), all its enumerated rows are deleted, same as the existing Enumerate behavior.
* Unchecking Multiple, or clearing Enumerate, also clears the enumerating items expression.
* Same authoring and performance guidance as other Arena expressions applies: keep the expression simple, since it's re-evaluated whenever its source data changes.

sections.text:
Expressions are used to determine value. The resulting value is usually one of various primitive types, such as numerical, string (text), Boolean, or complex data type.
Expressions can be defined using the “basic” expression editor and an “advanced” editor; the basic editor is easier to use and allows to define most of the expressions you will need in Arena. The generated expression will be a JavaScript expression.
The basic expression editor lets users define binary expressions, such as variable == some_value. For each operand, users can specify whether it is a constant value, a survey attribute, or a function.

When Variable is selected, the user can select the variable/attribute from a dropdown list; when constant is defined, depending on the attribute where the expression is defined, the value can be inserted in a text field or selected using a dropdown list (e.g. if the attribute is a code attribute, the constant value can be selected among the possible values in the related category).

sections.text:
7.5.1.        Working with categories
Categories define predefined lists of coded values that are used across the survey to provide consistent options for data entry, processing, and reporting. These fields are set up in accordance with pre-defined classification schemes. However, the Survey Administrator is free to add, remove or modify them. Code lists can be used to classify a wide range of attributes such as administrative levels, personnel, topographic elements, accessibility, land use classes, ownership and many more.

There can be two types of code lists: flat or hierarchical tables. A flat table contains only one level with two columns: code and label (or labels in all selected languages). A hierarchical code list can be used - for example - for storing data by administrative units (e.g., province, district, village).
Categories (as well as taxonomies) are common for all cycles, in case of a multi-cycle survey.
Command buttons

Adding a new category
New code lists can be added in two ways: "manually" or by importing a table in CSV/Excel format.
To add a new code list, click on the   button. Then add the Category name.

The category names should be unique. If the category name exists, there will be an error message, as follows.

A quicker option to create a new code list is to import them using a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file. The CSV file should be in Unicode (UTF-8) format.

sections.title: Categories (2/2)
sections.text:
Category tables can contain extra information (i.e. Extra properties), and they can work as lookup tables. This ancillary data can be retrieved from other sources, for example from GIS.
Extra properties can be used for example in the "Items filter" expressions (Examples of expressions) and in data analysis with R.

The next image shows hierarchical data in a CSV file. This can be used to import ancillary data for clusters (level1) and plots (level2).

The extra properties can contain the following types of data: text, numeric or geometry point. In case of geometry point (i.e., coordinates), the spatial reference system (SRS) must be preset into the survey (see the Arena Dashboard section in this manual). A coordinate data split into three columns looks like this:

The best method of getting this type of ancillary data table into Arena is to create the table in MS Excel, Libre Calc (or equal), save it as a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file and then import it. While importing, Arena asks to select data type for each column because the default data type is ‘text’.
In the data analysis with R, all categorical tables are accessible (as a list of data frames).
7.5.3.        Sampling Point Data
Sampling Point Data (SPD) table is a special hierarchical code list with a fixed category name "sampling_point_data". It can be used to define the list of sampling points, and their properties such as coordinates of each sample’s location. Sampling point locations can be viewed on the Arena Map.

Here is an example of a Sampling Point Data for a forest inventory case:

* levelX_code columns: 1 column for each level X (maximum 3 levels, e.g. if you have 2 levels, cluster and plot, you will have a column "level1_code" with cluster id value and a column "level2_code" for plot id value);
* label_LANGUAGECODE columns: labels that will be associated to each item on the list; e.g. label_en for English, label_fr for French; [6]
* description_LANGUAGECODE column: not needed, you can leave this blank!
* location_x, location_y, location_srs columns: geometry point data as shown above;
* optional: extra properties.

A spatial sampling point grid can be made in any GIS application, or by using a Plot Grid Generator, see Annex 6 for more information.

See the chapter Examples of expressions how to use and call Sampling Point Data with the help of expressions in a survey.

sections.text:
In Categories, use ‘Clone Category From Another Survey’ (next to Add, Export All, and Batch import). Pick a Source survey, then a Source category from that survey's category list, and confirm.
Arena checks the source category against the categories already in the current survey before cloning:
* If a category with the same internal ID already exists (i.e. this exact category was cloned into this survey before, even if since renamed), cloning is blocked with a message identifying it by its current name.
* If a different category already has the same name, cloning is blocked with a name-clash message.
* Otherwise, the category and its levels/items are copied into the current survey as a new, independent category.

sections.title: Working with taxonomies (1/2)
sections.text:
This section allows the user to add one or more species lists by uploading a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file. The list should contain all the taxonomic species that the user will select from during data entry. Species lists should be as comprehensive as possible and should be created using all resources available in the country: local or global databases, taxonomical books, experts’ knowledge etc. For security reasons it will not be possible to add species during data entry. Instead, additional species should be added to the CSV/Excel file (by a Survey Administrator) and the updated species list uploaded to Arena.
In case of a multi-cycle survey, Taxonomies (as well as Categories) are common across cycles.
Adding a Species list:
A species list table should be prepared in advance following the formatting requirements indicated below.
The columns are as follows:
* code (required): alphanumeric (i.e. letters and numerals) unique identifier code associated to the species,
* family (optional): family name of the species,
* genus (optional): genus of the species,
* scientific_name (required): latin name of the species (genus + [optionally] species name + [optionally] subspecies name e.g. Pinus spp. or Pinus radiata),
* lat (optional): synonym(s)[7],
* vernacular_name (optional): such as local name or a timber trade name. The vernacular name column must be named with the ISO 639-2 language code of the corresponding language (e.g. eng for English, swa for Swahili, etc.). So, the column name in the imported file is just the language code.

sections.text:
Currently, only a System Administrator of FAO can add new templates into Arena. If you are a Survey Administrator, and you want to offer a new template into Arena or improve an existing one, please contact the Arena development team by an email: openforisinitiative@gmail.com, write into the Topic field: "Suggested survey to Arena template".

sections.title: What are the data entry stages?
sections.text:
Arena implements a workflow which divides data processing into three steps (or stages): 1) data entry, 2) data cleansing, and 3) data analysis.

            1. Data entry stage
               * Data are entered into the system exactly as they appear on paper field forms.
               * They are neither interpreted nor corrected during this phase.
               * Invalid values (those marked as "error") must be checked against the field forms. If the value was copied correctly, the value should be manually accepted. If it was copied incorrectly, the value should be entered as it appears on the field forms.
               * Once all errors are either resolved or confirmed, the data entry clerk submits the record for data cleansing.  Before entering the cleansing phase, a copy is made and marked read-only. No further changes may be made to this record by data entry staff (unless the record is returned by data cleansing staff).
               2. Data cleansing stage
                  * Experts with knowledge of field conditions and data work with a copy of the data entered at step 1 to correct or remove invalid values.
Note: "Data entry" level users cannot edit the data which is at the cleansing stage.
                  * If the data cleansing expert deems that the data entry task was not completed or that the record contains too many errors, the record may be returned to phase 1 (entry) for additional changes.
                  * Once all data errors are resolved, the record may then be submitted for data analysis.  This locks the record so that no further changes may be made.
                     3. Data analysis stage
                        * Records are locked. They can be viewed but not edited.
                        * Records ready for analysis.
                        * If during analysis data are deemed incomplete or incorrect, the record may be rejected and sent back for further cleansing. Once updated and resubmitted, the record may once again be available for calculation and analysis.

Importing data from CSV or Excel file (1/2)

Data to be imported must be provided as a .CSV (in Unicode, UTF-8; column separator is comma) or Excel file (.xlsx). Each file to be imported can contain data of one entity. The data entry contains several steps.

STEP 1. Select the cycle
In case of a multicycle survey, the user has to select the target cycle (read more about cycles here).

STEP 2. Select Import Type gives two options as follows:

For example, in the following survey "CLUSTER" is the root level entity, and a file to be imported should contain "cluster data" only.

To bring the files themselves into Arena together with the tabular data:
                                          1. Prepare a folder where you will put both the data file in tabular format (CSV/Excel file) and all the files referenced in the file-attribute column(s) of your data file;

2. Copy the data file (.csv or .xlsx) inside the just prepared folder;

sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .collect-data format.
If a survey is created in OF Collect, and this survey is imported into Arena and published, data can also be imported into the Arena (later). This enables collection of data using OF Collect Mobile in data collection.

The checkbox "delete all records before import" means that all records (of the selected cycle) in the target survey will be deleted. Be cautious while using this selection!
Selection "Force import from another survey" allows importing data from a collect-data file, which may have different survey name in Collect than in Arena, but the same schema (i.e. source and target schemas match).

sections.title: Import data from Arena/Arena Mobile file
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .zip format and earlier exported from Arena or Arena Mobile. The survey structures must match between the target survey and in the file to be imported.
The conflict resolution strategy means that the user needs to decide what to do in a case where the same record, or a record with the same key attributes, is already in the database.
  It contains three options:
                                          1. Skip the record if it already exists in the database,
                                          2. Overwrite the record with the imported data,
                                          3. Merge the records. This means that the data from the imported file will be attached to the record. By this means, for example a missing tree (entity) data can be imported into the records.

sections.title: Validation report
sections.text:
Errors in data can be detected by several means. While editing the data in Data Records, there can be an error message    indicating that there is something wrong in the data. However, there is no easy way to find the erroneous data in the Data Records. So, for searching and browsing the erroneous data, we should use the Validation Report tool.
The data validation report is a table that is created by running through all data validation checks in the survey. It is essential to run this report and fix all errors in the data before the data enters the Analysis phase. Note: if your data is already at the Analysis step   , you cannot edit the records. You need to submit the record back to Step 2.
In case of a multi-cycle dataset, the validation is executed for the selected cycle’s data only.
The validation report can look as follows:

The validation report shows all records that have issues, either ‘Warning’ or ‘Error’. The Error message will be automatically generated, if the custom "Error Message" is left blank in the survey designing phase.
The erroneous records can be directly accessed and edited from the Validation Report view.
The validation report can be exported into an Excel file by clicking on the   button. The report contains more information than the screen view, and it looks in MS Excel as follows.

sections.title: Merging data (1/2)
sections.text:
Records can be merged into one. This feature works only when it's applied to 2 records at a time.
The records to merge can be selected on the records list, then press the Merge button on the top bar.
Merging data can be quite useful when, for example, data on the same site is collected using different devices; Arena and Arena Mobile don't allow creating records with the same identifiers (keys), but to make the data collection in the field faster, users can work on the same site (cluster) with different devices and combine the data later on. sections.text:
To export a printable document of a record, follow the next steps:
                                          1. Open a record in Data → Records.
                                          2. Navigate to the page you want to print. This is only needed when printing the current page.

Option
	Explanation
	Format
	PDF or Word (.docx). The Word file can be edited further before printing.
	Content
	Full survey: the whole record, with the survey label and description as the title. Current page only: only the entity instance currently shown in the form (e.g. the plot or tree you are viewing), with the entity label as the title. Its subpages are not included.
	Include QR code
	Adds a QR code to the first page. Available only with "Current page only".
	Page orientation
	Portrait or Landscape. The selection will be the document default. Entities with their own orientation set in the Print tab override it.
	The document is generated in the language currently selected in the form's language selector, and for the cycle of the record. The downloaded file is named after the survey, the cycle and, for "Current page only", the entity label.

What is included in the document
                                          * The layout follows the Form Designer. Attributes are placed according to the form grid (columns and positions). Multiple entities displayed as tables are printed as tables. Multiple entities displayed as forms are printed once per instance, each under its own heading.
                                          * Entities on their own page, and multiple entities at the upper levels of the hierarchy, start on a new page.

                                          * Image file attributes are printed as pictures. Other file types show the file name.
                                          * Attributes set as Hide in entry form, and nodes that are not relevant or not visible in the record, are not printed.

sections.title: QR code
sections.text:
When the "Include QR code" option is enabled, Arena stores a read-only PDF copy of the exported page on the server and prints a QR code in the top-right corner of the first page. Scanning the QR code with any smartphone opens the stored PDF.
                                          * The link is valid for one year.
                                          * Exporting the same page again with the QR code option updates the stored PDF with the current data and extends the validity by another year. The QR code and its link remain unchanged, ensuring that previously printed copies continue to work.
                                          * The QR link can be accessed without logging in to Arena. Anyone who has the printed document can view that page's data. Therefore, carefully consider whether to use this feature for records containing personal, confidential, or otherwise sensitive information.

sections.title: Creating a processing chain (1/2)
sections.text:
Data processing in Arena is implemented using R scripts. Each survey has its own set of scripts, which can be created and modified by the Survey Administrator or Data Analyst. The processing can be executed either in a cloud-based RStudio environment or locally using R and RStudio installed on a personal computer, which is the recommended approach.

Data processing is carried out through a calculation chain consisting of the result variables to be calculated. Each computation within the chain is referred to in this manual as a calculation step. While a survey can contain several calculation chains, only one chain can be designated for applying the Sampling Design and Statistical Analysis methods.
Advantages of the processing chain
                                          * Automated calculation result attributes (e.g., tree volume, biomass, carbon),
                                          * One script – it is transparent and easy to repeat,
                                          * R provides powerful statistical engine,
                                          * Efficiency and reproducibility of inventory workflows by standardizing processing steps,
                                          * Provides a foundation for reporting and documentation.
The concept of using a data processing chain in sampling-based assessment is illustrated in the following chart.

Important: about using R packages
                                                   * Whenever possible, load all your required packages in 004-common.R, as this provides a single location for managing package dependencies and simplifies script maintenance.

                                                   * When using additional packages, avoid loading them with the library() function. Instead, use the usePackage() function, for example:
usePackage("lmfor")
The usePackage() function checks whether the specified package is already installed. If the package is not available, it is installed automatically. The function is defined in the system file init-packages.R:

 dplyr::select(),  dplyr::filter()
This practice improves code readability and helps ensure that the intended function is used when multiple packages provide functions with the same name.

                                                      11. The scripts located in the user/ and sampling/ folders are the primary files that require user-developed code.

Within the RStudio project, survey data are organized into data frames corresponding to each entity. In addition, two lists of data frames are available: categories and taxonomies.
For example, if the survey includes a code list named land_use, it can be accessed as categories$land_use.
Taxonomic tables may also contain additional attributes, such as species-specific wood density values. Since these attributes are stored as character fields in Arena, they must be converted to numeric data types before being used in calculations.

13. RStudio Server users: After the processing has completed successfully, close your RStudio session by returning to Arena and selecting the option to terminate the RStudio connection from the main side panel.

Terminating the connection frees server resources and makes them available to other users of the cloud-based RStudio service.

If RStudio Server does not start
If you encounter an error message like the one shown below in your web browser, it indicates that the RStudio Server instance is currently unable to start.

In such cases, please wait 5 to 10 minutes and try again. This issue may occur when many users are attempting to access the system simultaneously, resulting in limited server resources.
Working with external files (e.g. CSVs and image files)
If you are using RStudio Server and need to create or save files during your session, such as CSV files, images, or other outputs, please refer to Annex 3 for detailed instructions.
Error handling
In arena.R, each module invocation within the processing chain includes an argument for capturing and handling errors, as illustrated in the example below.

All errors encountered during script execution are collected in a global error log. This log is evaluated by the script system/persist-user-scripts.R when user-developed R scripts are saved back to the Arena server. If any errors are present in the log, execution of the calculation chain is halted and a warning message is displayed in the R Console. All reported errors must be resolved before the chain can be executed successfully.
After fixing the erroneous R code, the error log must be cleared before rerunning the scripts. There are three ways to do this:
                                                      1. Restart the chain from system/init.R.
This clears the error log automatically. However, the survey data needs to be reloaded from the Arena server into RStudio, which may take considerable time for large datasets.
                                                      2. Run cleanGlobalErrors() in the R Console.
After clearing the error log, rerun the chain starting from the corrected script or module.
                                                      3. Add cleanGlobalErrors() to 000-common.R.
By including this command in 000-common.R, the error log will be cleared automatically when you rerun the chain from that point.
Choosing the second or third option is often more efficient, as it avoids reloading data from the server and reduces processing time during script development and testing.
Problems with system/persist-results.R
IIn some cases, computed results cannot be written back to the Arena database. One common cause is the presence of one or more data frame columns that contain only NA values. When this occurs, error messages similar to the examples below may be displayed.

Or the error message is this one:

The first step is to inspect the result variables and verify whether any of them contain only NA values. If all result variables appear valid, the issue may originate from the input data retrieved from Arena.
A practical solution is to remove any columns that consist entirely of missing values before rerunning the result persistence process. For example, if the error occurs in the tree data frame, the following command removes all columns whose values are exclusively NA:
tree[sapply(tree, function(x) all(is.na(x)))] <- NULL
After removing the affected columns, rerun the system/persist-results.R script to write the results back to the Arena database.
Viewing updated scripts in Arena
User scripts are saved back to the Arena database by the system/persist-user-scripts.R script.
If an updated script is not immediately visible in the Arena script editor, refresh your web browser to reload the latest version from the database.

sections.title: Sampling design and statistical analytics
sections.text:
10.4.1.        Sampling strategy
This section will cover defining a sample strategy in Arena. A sample strategy is the combination of sample design along with an estimator (formula) from which is calculated an estimate for a parameter of interest. For many strategies the sample design and formula are so closely associated that the term "design" is used when "strategy" is meant, we will follow this convention.
Arena supports the following sampling strategies: 1) simple random sampling and systematic sampling;
2) stratified sampling; and 3) single stage or cluster sampling. In addition, the script can compute area estimates for 4) two-phase sampling (UNDER DEVELOPMENT, non-clustered, or clustered).

Definitions and Background
Most forest inventory measurement protocols use a set of circles or rectangles; the set is arranged geometrically around the sample point for the set, see figure below.

In a majority of inventories, the set is referred to as a cluster and individual elements are referred to as plots. One exception is the Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) program of the United States Forest Service, which refers to the set as a plot and individual elements as subplots. To avoid confusion between the two uses of "plot" we will refer to the FIA set as the FIA-plot.
In Open Foris Calc, the smallest unit of measured area is called a base unit, and it is assumed that the base unit is of a single stand type. For many inventories the plot is the base unit. Although in some inventories the plot can be mapped into different stand types. One example of this is FIA, which has the field crews divide the subplots into different stands if there is a stand boundary which can be repeatable mapped.

Typically, trees are measured on clusters of plots, where the plots may vary in size and/or number depending on the diameter class of the tree.  Therefore, each entity that contains "area-based" variable(s) gets a new result attribute automatically in a processing chain, for example "tree" gets attribute "tree_plot_area_".

Areas of strata
Stratified sampling requires computation of inclusion probabilities by stratum. In Arena, inclusion probabilities are expressed as "expansion factors" (which are equal to the inverse of inclusion probability).
There are two methods in Arena script to compute expansion factor for a base unit:
                                                         1. Computation with the help of sample weights in stratum, i.e.

                                                         2. Areas of stratum is known, i.e.

Method A does not allow you to compute "Totals" (such as total volume, biomass) correctly. However, per hectare results can be computed.

If the extent of samples is known (such as sampling plot areas in forest inventories), Arena’s script can always compute results per hectare basis, such as tree volume per hectare. sections.title: Non-response bias corrections
sections.text:
A problem common to nearly all sample-based surveys is partial or complete non-response from some of the selected sample units. Arena script can apply the Weighting Class Adjustment method and compute weight adjustment factors based on data about the planned number of sampling units. In this case, missing observations are ignored and an adjustment factor is incorporated into a sample weight to compensate for non-response or situations where all or part of a sample (plot) falls outside the population.
The weight adjustment requires information about the planned number of Primary Sampling Units (PSUs) and Secondary Sampling Units (SSUs).
In a forest inventory, Primary Sampling Units can be sample plots or clusters, by strata in case of stratified sampling. Secondary Sampling Units can be sample plots.
In stratified sampling, the number of PSUs and SSUs are given within the stratum attribute’s category table, as follows:

In the example above, the area of Stratum 1 is 30 ha, and the initial number of clusters (PSUs) is 85, and the number of sample plots in a cluster is 4.
In the next example, the non-response bias correction is not computed for missing clusters, but only for missing sample plots (SSUs):

And in the next example, the non-response bias correction is computed only for missing clusters (PSUs) in strata, but not for sample plots (SSUs):

If this lookup table is missing or its format is incorrect, Arena’s R script cannot compute corrections.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (1/2)
sections.text:
Arenalytics is an analytical dashboard developed for reporting and exploring data collected and processed with Open Foris Arena. It was designed to address one of the main challenges of sample-based assessments: generating reliable statistics, tables, and figures from large and complex survey datasets without requiring users to predefine all reporting outputs in advance. The dashboard was developed particularly for forest inventories and other sample-based assessments where users need to produce estimates such as biomass, tree density, volume, carbon stocks, or other indicators across multiple reporting domains. The dashboard allows users to dynamically analyse survey results by selecting measures, dimensions, and filters, producing estimates, totals, means, and reliability statistics on demand.

The Arenalytics workflow begins in Open Foris Arena, where survey data are collected and processed using a calculation chain. Once the processing chain has been executed in RStudio, Arena automatically generates Minimum Area Unit (MAU) files that contain pre-computed result variables and supporting attributes required for reporting. These files are packaged into a ZIP archive and loaded into Arenalytics for analysis.
After loading a MAU zip file, Arenalytics performs automatic validation checks and provides a survey summary to help users verify that the uploaded data are ready for analysis. Users can then select an entity, choose one or more measures to analyse, and define dimensions and filters that determine how results will be aggregated and presented. Dimensions can originate from either the original survey data or from the processing chain, enabling flexible reporting across administrative units, forest types, diameter classes, species groups, and many other categories. The resulting tables are generated instantly and updated whenever the settings in the ‘Cross outputs settings’ section change.

Workflow Summary:
Arena Survey with Data and Processing Chain
→ Run Chain in RStudio
 → Generate MAU ZIP file
   → Load data into Arenalytics
     → Select Entity and Dimensions
        → Click Run analysis
         → Select Measures and Filters
           → Review & Export results
             → Create figures
               → Generate reports
	The dashboard can be accessed through a web application or installed locally from its open-source R package, making it suitable for both online and offline environments:
                                                                  1. Use the online version. Open the hosted dashboard in your web browser: https://openforis-shiny.shinyapps.io/arenalytics/
                                                                  2. RECOMMENDED: Install and run locally in a Rstudio instance with
if (!require(remotes)) install.packages("remotes")
if (!require(arenalytics)) remotes::install_github("openforis/arenalytics", upgrade="never")
arenalytics::shiny_run_arenalytics()

The internal showcase presentation also notes that a demo dataset is available in the About section of the application.
The outcome of the Arena processing chain is a ZIP file of semi-aggregated data that will serve as input for Arenalytics, a Minimum Area Unit (MAU) file. The MAU file contains data aggregated to the Minimum Area Unit level, which is defined as the smallest homogeneous land unit in the survey area. In the Arena processing chain, the MAU is equivalent to the base unit used for statistical estimation.
Examples:
                                                                  * If a plot is completely homogeneous (single land use or vegetation type), the plot itself is the MAU.
                                                                  * If a plot is divided into several land-use or vegetation sections, then each homogeneous section becomes a separate MAU unit. Estimation variables are first computed for these sections and then aggregated to higher reporting levels.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (2/2)
sections.text:
The MAU file is automatically generated by an Arena system script as a ZIP file. It contains:
                                                                  * Result estimates for each base unit (MAU).
                                                                  * All relevant dimensions derived from categorical, taxonomic, and Boolean attributes.
                                                                  * Pre-computed measures that Arenalytics can subsequently aggregate into tables, charts, means, totals, and sampling-error estimates for any user-selected combination of dimensions.
Arenalytics reads measures at the MAU level and dynamically aggregates them to any reporting level (forest type, species, administrative region, diameter class, etc.) requested by the user. For a typical forest inventory case, where plots may be split into land-use strata or forest types, you can think of the MAU file as a dataset where each record represents one homogeneous plot section together with all its computed area-based variables and reporting dimensions.
The generated MAU ZIP file can be stored on the Arena server to facilitate archiving and future retrieval. Follow these steps:

sections.title: Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text: This chapter explains how to copy an existing processing chain with R scripts from one survey into another without rebuilding a new chain step by step.

sections.title: Overview
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey

sections.title: Prerequisites
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
* You must have Survey Administrator or Data Analyst permissions in the destination survey (the one you want to copy the chain into).
                                                                     * You must also have access to the source survey (the one the chain is copied from). Only surveys you can access, and that already contain at least one chain, are offered as a source.
                                                                     * The destination survey should already contain the entities that the source chain's calculated variables refer to (for example, plot or tree), using the same entity names. Arena checks this for you before the clone runs; if the entities do not exist in the target survey, the analysis variables associated to those entities won’t be cloned.

sections.title: Step-by-step: cloning a chain
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
1. Open the destination survey (the survey you want the chain copied into) and go to Analysis → Chains.
                                                                     2. In the Chains panel, click the button “Clone from another survey”.
                                                                     3. In the Clone chain from another survey dialog, select the Source survey (or template) from the dropdown list. Only surveys and templates you have access to, and that contain at least one chain, appear here.
                                                                     4. Select the Source chain you want to copy from the list of chains available in that survey.
                                                                     5. Arena automatically runs a compatibility check, comparing the entities used by the source chain's calculation steps with the entities available in the destination survey.
                                                                     6. Review the compatibility results. If everything is compatible, confirm the clone by clicking Clone.
                                                                     7. Arena creates the new chain in the destination survey, copies the scripts and calculated variables, and then opens the newly created chain automatically so you can review it.

sections.title: What happens after cloning
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
* A new chain is created in the destination survey with a new, unique identifier, it is entirely separate from the source chain.
                                                                     * All R scripts from the source chain are copied over as-is; you can edit them afterwards like any other chain script.
                                                                     * Calculated variables are re-created under the matching entities of the destination survey, together with any categories or taxonomies they depend on.
                                                                     * The new chain is validated automatically once created, and any issues (for example, an expression referencing an attribute that does not exist in the destination survey) are flagged for you to resolve, the same way validation works for a chain you build manually.
                                                                     * You are         taken directly to the newly created chain, ready for review, adjustment, and publishing.

sections.title: Notes and limitations
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
* Cloning copies the chain definition and scripts; it does not copy previously computed results or published data — you still need to run the chain in RStudio to generate results in the destination survey.
                                                                     * Only chains you can access (i.e., chains belonging to surveys you are a member of) can be used as a source.
                                                                     * If the source and destination surveys use different names for otherwise equivalent entities, rename the entity in one of the two surveys first so the compatibility check can match them.
                                                                     * A survey can contain more than one chain; cloning adds a new chain alongside any chains that already exist in the destination survey; it does not replace them.

sections.title: User Grouping
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey

sections.title: Overview
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A Survey Administrator can organize the people who collect data for a survey into named groups (e.g., by region, team, or organization). A group can optionally carry one or more qualifiers (key/value pairs that automatically restrict and pre-fill the data that its members collect) so that each group only can see and edit the records that belong to them.
User Groups are useful when:
                                                                     * Several field teams share the same survey but should not see or edit each other’s records.
                                                                     * Records must be automatically tagged with a region, project, or organization code as soon as they are created, based on who is entering the data.
                                                                     * You want to get a quick overview of which users are assigned to which team, and a method to reassign them.

sections.title: Accessing User Groups
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
Only users with a Survey Administrator role in the current survey can create, edit, delete groups, or manage members.
User Groups are managed per survey, via the Users section of the survey menu:
                                                                     1. Select the survey and go to Users on the left-hand side menu.
                                                                     2. Select the User Groups tab.
The User Groups page has up to three tabs, depending on your permissions:
Tab
	What it shows
	User Groups
	A simple list of the groups defined in the survey.
	Group Assignments
	A Kanban-style board with one column per group (plus an "Unassigned" column) and one card per user; drag and drop a user’s card to change their group.
	Members Report
	A flat table with one row per group member, listing the group’s name, label and qualifiers alongside the member’s name, email, survey role and account status.

sections.title: Creating and Editing a User Group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
1. On the User Groups tab, click New Group.
                                                                     2. Enter a Name for the group. The name is normalized automatically (no spaces or special characters) and it must be unique within the survey.
                                                                     3. Enter a Label for each survey language – this is the friendly name shown to users throughout Arena.
                                                                     4. Optionally add one or more Qualifiers (see section 4 below).
                                                                     5. Click Save. Once the group is saved, a Members panel appears at the bottom of the page (see section 5).

To edit an existing group, open it from the User Groups list and change any field, then click Save again. To remove a group, open it and click Delete; in this case the members are not deleted, they simply become unassigned.

sections.title: Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: A qualifier is a key/value pair attached to a group. The key must match the name of a survey attribute that has been marked as a qualifier attribute in the Form Designer (see 4.1). When this is done, Arena uses the pair to automatically fill in and restrict data for members of that group.

sections.title: Marking an attribute as a Qualifier
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be used as qualifiers. To enable one, do next:
                                                                     1. Open the Form Designer and select the text or code attribute (it must be defined inside the root level entity) that will hold the group value (for example, "region" or "project_code").
                                                                        2. In the attribute’s Basic Properties panel, enable the Qualifier checkbox. This option only appears once when at least one User Group exists in the survey.
What "Qualifier" does: When a new record is created by a user belonging to a group, this attribute is automatically filled with the value specified for it among that group’s qualifiers. Users will only be able to see and modify records belonging to their own group if they belong to one.

sections.title: Adding qualifier values to a group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Back on the group’s edit page, in the Qualifiers panel:
                                                                        1. Click Add qualifier.
                                                                        2. Under Key, enter the exact name of the qualifier attribute defined on the form (e.g. "region").
                                                                        3. Under Value, enter the value that should apply to this group (e.g. "North"; for a Code attribute, enter the item’s code).
                                                                        4. Repeat for additional qualifier attributes, and then click Save.
A group can have several qualifiers if the form defines several qualifier attributes. Each qualifier key must be unique within the group, and it cannot be left blank.

sections.title: Effect on data entry and data access
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
* New record: the qualifier attribute(s) are filled in automatically as soon as a member of the group starts collecting a new record, using the value(s) set on their group.
                                                                        * Existing records: a user can only view and edit records whose qualifier attribute value matches their own group’s qualifier value. Attempts to open or edit a record outside their group are rejected.
                                                                        * Unassigned users, or groups without a matching qualifier, are not restricted by this mechanism.
                                                                        * A user is considered to belong to at most one group per survey; only that group’s qualifiers are applied.

sections.title: Managing Group Members
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: There are two ways to assign survey users to a group. These are explained next.

sections.title: Method 1. From the group’s edit page
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
1. Open the group and scroll to the Members panel.
                                                                        2. Use the Add member dropdown to pick up a survey user by name and email.
                                                                        3. If the chosen user already belongs to a different group, Arena asks for confirmation before moving them (a user can only be a member of one group at a time).
                                                                        4. To remove a member, click the ✕ icon next to their name. They become unassigned, not deleted from the survey.

sections.title: Method 2. From the Group Assignments board (drag and drop)
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The Group Assignments tab (visible only to users who can manage groups) shows every survey user as a card on a Kanban-style board, with one column per group plus a leading Unassigned column.
                                                                        1. Go to Users > User Groups > Group Assignments.
                                                                        2. Drag a user’s card from its current column into the column of the group you want to assign them to (or into Unassigned to remove them from any group).
The new status is saved immediately; there is no separate Save step for this view.

sections.title: Members Report
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: The Members Report tab gives a flat, exportable-style view for auditing group membership: one row per group/member pair, showing the group’s name, label and qualifiers next to the member’s name, email, survey role and account status (Invited, Accepted, or Password change required). Groups with no members still appear, with a single empty-member row, so no group is missed.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
* Can a user belong to more than one group?
No. Adding a user to a group who already belongs to a different group moves them to the new group after a confirmation prompt.
                                                                        * What happens to a group’s members if the group is deleted?
They are not removed from the survey; they simply become unassigned and lose any qualifier restriction that the group applied.
                                                                        * Can I use a multiple-choice or nested attribute as a qualifier?
No. Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be marked as qualifiers.

How to avoid performance issues with Arena / Arena Mobile
If you encounter slowness while editing a large number of entities in a multiple entity (table), you should check the expressions set in for every attribute (default values, validation rules, etc.), because, depending on the way they are defined, they can be evaluated by Arena and Arena Mobile too many times. sections.title: RStudio Server: writing and downloading files created during run-time
sections.text:
Because RStudio Server works on a remote server, getting files, such as CSV files or graphic files, created by the R scripts from the server to the user’s machine requires special methods. Here we go through how to do this.

                                                                              1. Write this script into 004-common.R:
# define a folder for output files
user_file_path <- './user_output/'

# create a folder for files to be exported
if (!dir.exists( user_file_path )) dir.create( user_file_path, showWarnings = FALSE )

cat( normalizePath(user_file_path) )

Optionally, you can also use a function to add all "user’s files" into a zip file (arena_R_export.zip) which can be downloaded (after running the project files). Add also this script into 004-common.R (after the script above):

zip_user_files <- function(tFolder) {
  #delete zip if it exists (i.e., file to be downloaded)
  fn <- paste0( tFolder, "arena_R_export.zip ")
  if (file.exists(fn)) {
    #Delete file if it exists
    file.remove(fn)
  }

  # check if any files to be zipped
  f <- list.files(tFolder, all.files=TRUE, recursive=TRUE, full.names=FALSE)
  if (length(f) > 0) {
    zip::zip("arena_R_export.zip", f, recurse=TRUE , root=tFolder, include_directories = TRUE,
           mode = "mirror")
  }
}

Note: add script
        zip_user_files( user_file_path )
into the very last calculation step.

                                                                              2. in the part where you need to write something into a CSV file, use this type of command line

write.csv(my_DF, paste0( user_file_path, "test.csv" ), row.names = FALSE)

                                                                              3. To download the files from the server, there are two methods:
a) using RStudio’s EXPORT tool (this is easier),
b) or by R coding.
a) RStudio’s EXPORT tool:
In the Files pane, More menu, there is an Export… option:

b) Coding method to export the files from the server:
file_list = list.files(path=user_file_path, pattern="*.csv")
for (i in seq_along(file_list)) {
    export_filename = file_list[[i]]

    # create a path for file to export
    my_export_file_path <- paste0(user_file_path, export_filename)

    # make a pause before exporting the next file, otherwise there can be a pop-up warning
    if (i > 1) {
       cat('*** PRESS ENTER HERE')
      readLines(stdin(), 1)
