sections.title: Installing Open Foris Arena on a Custom Server (1/2)
sections.text:
This section explains how to install and run Open Foris Arena on your own server (on-premises or cloud VM) using Docker, instead of using the hosted openforis-arena.org platform. It is intended for system administrators who will maintain the server.
1. Overview
Arena is distributed as a set of Docker images: the Arena application itself, a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database, and, optionally, an RStudio Server container used for running custom R scripts on collected data. Running Arena on a custom server therefore requires Docker and, unless you already have one, a PostgreSQL database.
2. Prerequisites
                                                                                 * A server (Linux is recommended) with a public or reachable IP address, if the server must be accessed outside the local network.
                                                                                 * Docker installed. Download and install it from docker.com if it is not already present.
                                                                                 * Sufficient disk space for the database, uploaded files, and analysis output directories.
                                                                                 * Network access from the server to the internet, to pull Docker images (or a local copy of the images if the server is offline).
                                                                                 * Optional: an SMTP or SendGrid/Office365/Amazon SES account, if Arena should send emails (e.g., password resets, survey invitations).
3. Install and configure PostgreSQL
If you do not already have a PostgreSQL database available, run one as a Docker container. The following command creates a database named "arena" and a user "arena" with password "arena", listening on port 5444:
docker run -d --name arena-db -p 5444:5432 \
-e POSTGRES_DB=arena \
-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=arena \
-e POSTGRES_USER=arena \
postgis/postgis:17-3.5
Note: Change the database name, user, password, and port to suit your environment and security requirements. Arena can also be pointed at an already-existing PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance instead of a dedicated container.
4. Create the configuration file (arena.env)
Create a text file named arena.env containing the parameters Arena needs at startup. The most commonly used variables are listed below; the full list is available in the Arena GitHub repository.
Variable
	Purpose
	Example
	ARENA_PORT
	Port the web application listens on
	9090
	PGHOST / PGPORT / PGDATABASE / PGUSER / PGPASSWORD
	PostgreSQL connection parameters (or use DATABASE_URL)
	localhost / 5444 / arena / arena / arena
	TEMP_FOLDER
	Folder for temporary uploaded files
	/home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload
	FILE_STORAGE_PATH
	File-system folder for stored files (omit to use DB or S3)
	/home/your_user/openforis/arena/files
	ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR
	Folder shared with RStudio Server for analysis output
	/home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis
	USE_HTTPS
	Set to true if requests are forwarded to HTTPS by a reverse proxy
	false
	ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD
	Credentials for the first system administrator account
	admin@example.org / temporary-password

A minimal working arena.env looks like this:
ARENA_PORT=9090

PGHOST=localhost
PGPORT=5444
PGDATABASE=arena
PGUSER=arena
PGPASSWORD=arena

TEMP_FOLDER=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload
FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/files
ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis

USER_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-string
USE_HTTPS=false

ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.org
ADMIN_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-temporary-password
Security: ADMIN_PASSWORD is used only to create the first system administrator account. Change this password from within Arena immediately after the first login, and consider removing it from the file afterward.

5. Install and run Arena
From the folder containing arena.env, run:

sections.title: Installing Open Foris Arena on a Custom Server (2/2)
sections.text:
docker run --env-file ./arena.env --network="host" openforis/arena:latest
This pulls the official Arena image and starts the container, exposing the web application on the port defined by ARENA_PORT (9090 by default). Use the same command to restart Arena after it has been stopped.
6. Open Arena in the browser
Once the container is running, open:
http://localhost:9090
(replace localhost with the server's hostname or IP address if connecting remotely). The Arena login form should appear. On first startup, Arena automatically creates a system administrator account using ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from arena.env. Log in with those credentials and change the password using the Change Password function inside Arena.
7. Optional: run RStudio Server for statistical analysis
To enable custom R scripts and calculation chains, run RStudio Server as a separate container, sharing the ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR folder defined in arena.env:
docker run -d --name arena-rstudio --network=host \
-v ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR:/home/rstudio \
-e DISABLE_AUTH=true \
rocker/rstudio
Replace ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR with the actual path used in arena.env. RStudio Server will be available at:
http://localhost:8787
To restart RStudio Server after a reboot or stop:
docker container restart arena-rstudio
Alternatively, an already-existing external RStudio Server (or RStudio Server Pro pool) can be connected by setting RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL (and related RSTUDIO_* variables) in arena.env instead of running a local container.
8. Recommended next steps
                                                                                 * Configure HTTPS via a reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx or Traefik) in front of Arena, and set USE_HTTPS=true in arena.env.
                                                                                 * Set up an email service (SendGrid, Office365, or Amazon SES) so Arena can send account and survey-invitation emails.
                                                                                 * Schedule regular backups of the PostgreSQL database and the file-storage / analysis directories.
                                                                                 * Review         the ALLOW_USER_ACCESS_REQUEST, FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT, and JOB_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY settings to match your organization's needs.
